Colorado’s economic and business environments shift | Tatiana Bailey

📅 Nov 01, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

I’m not prone to exaggeration, so I thoughtfully state that I believe we are living through unusually transformational and precarious times. The pace of technological, geopolitical and economic change is unlike anything I’ve witnessed.

My husband recently sent a photo to the family group chat of a gasoline fill-up at $109. Gasoline and diesel prices have surged, with diesel nearly $6.40 a gallon. Virtually all goods are transported using diesel, so these prices touch almost everything we consume.

Prolonged conflict in the Middle East, tariffs and trade uncertainty further exacerbate inflation, probably keeping interest rates high. As of right now, the 30-year mortgage rate is roughly 7.5%, and experts forecast two more rate hikes from the Fed, which kept rates untouched at last week’s meeting.

Meanwhile, our increasingly K-shaped economy has provided overall resilience, with higher-income households spending while lower- and middle-income households struggle to maintain purchasing power. These lower-income groups are saving less and borrowing more.

Furthermore, artificial intelligence may represent the largest labor market transformation since industrialization.

In my view, the convergence of these forces creates an extraordinary level of economic uncertainty.

But Colorado faces additional headwinds.

Our high housing costs make attracting workers harder, and increasingly complex regulations raise concerns about business competitiveness.

Colorado Chamber of Commerce research found that 67% of surveyed businesses believe our state is headed in the wrong direction.

Colorado’s job growth has also slowed significantly. To be fair, the U.S. has a low-hire environment particularly affecting entry-level workers and AI-exposed occupations. The difference is that Colorado once outperformed the nation in population and employment growth, but that advantage has weakened considerably.

Hence, the central question is whether Colorado can remain competitive in a national milieu of extraordinary uncertainty and technological change.

This is the theme of our Annual State of the Economy event on Wednesday, which will be one day after the election and those impacts will also be discussed.

I’ll examine national, state and local economic conditions and forecasts. Timothy Wonhof, Colorado’s director of labor market information, will address industry employment trends.

Tatiana Bailey’s graph #2

Rachel Beck, executive director of the Colorado Chamber of Commerce Foundation, will discuss regulatory pressures, business costs and the Chamber’s 10-year growth plan.

And Jonathan Liebert, president of the Better Business Bureau of Southern Colorado, will share businesses’ experiences, including the adoption of AI. 

I hope to hear from readers of my articles and viewers of my TV segments. Please join us Wednesday from 2 to 4 p.m. at Garden of the Gods Resort, followed by a networking happy hour. Tickets are $50 plus fees, and registration is available at www.ddestrategies.org.

Tatiana Bailey is executive director of the nonprofit Data-Driven Economic Strategies. Other Gazette articles, TV segments, DDES monthly economic dashboards with technical explanations and how to sponsor their work can be found at ddestrategies.org.

Inde Navarrette put her upcoming Marvel role front and center during her first turn as host of Saturday Night Live, using her opening monologue to tease playing Rogue in X-Men—and to take a shot at Shane Gillis’ monologue from the previous episode.

Discussing the work required to get into “Marvel shape,” Navarrette delivered a callback to Gillis’ sexist opening remarks.

“So, every morning, I put on my little whore outfit and hit the gym,” she joked, drawing laughs from the studio audience.

The actress also addressed her “scream queen” debut as Nikki in Curry Barker’s Obsession. Navarrette insisted that she was “nothing like Nikki,” only for the monologue to reveal her boyfriend taped to his chair in the audience.

The opening brought several other cast members into the action. Marcello Hernandez modeled a sexy TSA-agent costume, while Kam Patterson appeared as Elizabeth Holmes. Jeremy Culhane dressed as Wolverine and pitched himself for the role in the upcoming Jake Schreier project referenced in the bit.

Veronika Slowikowska and Grace Reiter joined the parade as Kelly Clarkson and the mechanical singing bird involved in Clarkson’s online feud with a Brooklyn gift shop.

Ghosts, disastrous inventions and disruptive flyers

Navarrette’s first sketch paired her with Hernandez as the ghosts of two children from the 1930s aboard the Queen Mary. Their characters repeatedly distracted a tourist who was trying to learn where another ghost had hidden treasure.

Air travel provided the setup for another ensemble piece, a fake Delta commercial promoting “Delta Disruptive,” a special section reserved exclusively for unruly and irrational passengers.

Mikey Day played a traveler attempting to open an exit door while declaring, “This plane is made out of Israel.” Navarrette, meanwhile, impersonated the woman who became known on social media for insisting, “She is not real!”

She switched personas again for The Uninterested Woman Dating Show, playing Dane, one of the show’s so-called “fuckboy” contestants. Jane Wickline and Sarah Sherman appeared alongside her as fellow contestants.

One of the night’s darkest premises came in The Inventor. Navarrette played the widow of an inventor who returned home after his funeral to discover the creations he had left behind, including a robot called PD-44.

Six years later, she brought home a date played by Ben Marshall. The robot attacked him, ripping off his penis and blowing him up. Only then did Navarrette’s character understand that PD-44 stood for “Penis Destroyer”—and interpret the machine’s violent programming as proof of her late husband’s devotion.

“He did love me. My husband did love me after all,” she said while covered in blood.

Navarrette and Hernandez reunited for a Spanish soap-opera spoof built around an ill-fated product-placement assignment. Their characters were required to incorporate Sprite Cherry Lime Habanero into a dramatic scene, but the promotional effort quickly became a disaster for the brand.

The melodrama escalated until Hernandez’s character urged Navarrette’s to drink the soda in order to kill her unborn baby, which had been conceived by his brother.

ShowBiz Take

Navarrette’s hosting debut connected three different parts of her current screen profile in one appearance: the unsettling world of Obsession, the physical preparation for her forthcoming Rogue role and the anything-goes demands of live sketch comedy.

The Rogue reference was the night’s biggest forward-looking movie tease, but Navarrette kept it inside a joke rather than turning her monologue into a straightforward promotional stop. From there, the episode gave her sharply different assignments, including a 1930s ghost, a dating-show contestant, a soap star and a blood-covered widow discovering the brutal meaning behind a robot’s name.

The episode also marked another first: Gracie Abrams made her debut as Saturday Night Live’s musical guest on the same installment that introduced Navarrette as host.

Taika Waititi is answering the critical response to Klara and the Sun by pointing to a sharp split between reviewers and moviegoers.

The director posted the film’s poster on Instagram on Saturday, drawing attention to its Rotten Tomatoes scores. The image showed a 78 percent audience score alongside a 28 percent critics score.

Waititi said he has avoided reading reviews directed at him or his peers for nearly 15 years, but indicated that he still pays attention to audiences.

“I haven’t read a review of anything aimed at me or my peers in almost 15 years. But I do listen to the people,” he wrote. “So this Halloween, let’s spare a thought for those sad lost souls who couldn’t achieve their dreams of becoming artists, and thus became critics. The same people who also hated Jojo Rabbit. Irrelevant. Out of touch. Obsolete. In the bin.”

The blunt post arrives as Klara and the Sun faces a challenging theatrical start. The film, which opened in theaters the previous week, earned an estimated $725,000 during its opening weekend and debuted outside the top 10.

It launched in 880 theaters across North America. At the time of publication, its worldwide gross stood at approximately $1.7 million.

Inside Klara and the Sun

Waititi’s film is adapted from Kazuo Ishiguro’s 2021 novel of the same name. Set in a dystopian future, the story centers on an obsolete companion android attempting to form a connection with Josie, a young owner who is dealing with an illness.

Jenna Ortega and Amy Adams star in the film. Artificial intelligence is central to its premise through the story’s use of AI companions, a subject Waititi also addressed at the movie’s New York premiere earlier this month.

Speaking with The Hollywood Reporter, the filmmaker acknowledged the continuing discussion over how artificial intelligence could be used within the entertainment industry. Although he described some level of adoption as probably unavoidable, he drew a distinction between AI functioning as a tool and serving as a substitute for people.

“There’s a big discussion about AI coming in: Will people use it? How much will they use it? I know it’s probably inevitable that we end up using it in our industry, but as long as it’s used by humans as a tool, as opposed to a replacement — I don’t want to replace humans. I want to work with them,” Waititi said.

ShowBiz Take

Waititi’s Instagram response turns the film’s divided Rotten Tomatoes reception into the center of the conversation. Rather than addressing individual reviews, he is using the audience score to challenge the relevance of the broader critical verdict.

The 50-point difference between the two scores gives that argument a clear numerical hook: audiences represented on the platform were substantially more positive than critics at the time captured in the poster. Waititi’s reference to Jojo Rabbit also makes clear that he sees the latest reviews as part of a wider disconnect between critics and reactions he considers more meaningful.

At the same time, the film’s early box-office figures provide another measure of its reception. With an estimated $725,000 opening weekend from 880 North American theaters and a debut outside the top 10, Klara and the Sun began its theatrical run with modest commercial results.

For now, the film is generating two distinct discussions: one about the divide between critics and audiences, and another about AI’s place in stories and in the industry itself. Waititi has made his position on both subjects unusually direct—he is dismissing the negative critical consensus while arguing that artificial intelligence should support human work rather than replace it.

The post Taika Waititi Highlights Rotten Tomatoes Divide in ‘Klara and the Sun’ Review Pushback first appeared on ShowBiz.com.

North Korea sanctions drew defiance from Pyongyang on October 31, 2026, when a foreign ministry spokesperson said sanctions and pressure “may work on the weak but never on us.” The statement landed two days after attackers drained about $6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what analysts call the biggest crypto hack on record. Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis blame North Korea’s TraderTraitor hacking group for the theft, though the Pyongyang statement never mentioned the Binance breach.

Pyongyang Rejects Sanctions After the Binance Hack

The Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) carried the statement, which answered a joint declaration from 11 countries and the European Union. That declaration reaffirmed monitoring of North Korea’s activities under United Nations Security Council resolutions and welcomed fresh US, Australian and EU sanctions on cyber operations and overseas workers. The spokesperson called the push a “strategic failure” and insisted that North Korea sanctions will not change the country’s status as a nuclear weapons state.

How the $6.3 Billion Binance Crypto Heist Unfolded

TRM Labs reports that the attacker moved about $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets across ten blockchains, most of it within roughly 20 minutes after 20:05 UTC on October 29. Binance puts the affected total near $6.3 billion, has set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover losses and says user funds remain safe. The FBI and US Secret Service now work with the exchange, and President Donald Trump confirmed a US inquiry into a possible North Korean link. The heist dwarfs the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, which the FBI also pinned on North Korea.

What North Korea Sanctions Mean for Crypto Security

Experts say Pyongyang turned to crypto theft to raise foreign currency for its economy and nuclear program under tough UN sanctions. Chainalysis now links North Korea linked hackers to nearly 89% of reported crypto hack losses in 2026, which raises a hard question: do North Korea sanctions slow the regime, or does stolen crypto help it dodge them? Exchanges should respond by hardening wallet infrastructure, monitoring cross-chain withdrawals in real time and vetting remote IT staff, since investigators cite IT worker infiltration and executive impersonation as common tactics. Attribution still rests on blockchain analysis, so watch for official confirmation from US authorities.

Microsoft’s big buyout, Amazon’s trillion-dollar future, and an AI wearable reviews our show

📅 Oct 31, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Microsoft is offering buyouts to about 60,000 employees, about a quarter of its workforce, including some execs. Unlike the retirement program Microsoft offered in the spring, this one has no age or tenure requirement, and business leaders decide whether their groups take part.

On this week’s GeekWire Podcast, we discuss what’s behind the offer, why buyout stories draw so much interest from readers, and how it fits with a blockbuster quarter for Microsoft. That includes $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI, more than Microsoft made from Xbox or Bing.

Amazon CEO Andy Jassy predicts that AWS and Amazon’s stores business could each reach $1 trillion in annual revenue in the next five to 10 years. AWS grew 39% in the third quarter, its fastest pace in nearly five years, but Amazon’s profit fell short of expectations as the cost of its AI buildout and growing debt cut into earnings.

Todd also tests Amazon’s new Bee AI wearable, which listens to the first part of the show, summarizes the conversation and offers a critique of its own.

We talk about what it’s like to wear a device that records the people around you, a concern raised by a former AWS security engineer. John starts to come around on the device, with reservations about its shopping features.

Plus, our Halloween costumes, and a Trivia Challenge inspired by T-Mobile’s new T-Mix plans.

Remittances to Uzbekistan Reach $18.9bn as OSON X Opens a UAE Money App for Central Asians

📅 Oct 31, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

A new entrant on the UAE–Central Asia corridor seeks banking and infrastructure partners ahead of Dubai FinTech Summit

DUBAI, UAE, October 31st, 2026 — People from Central Asia who live and work in the UAE send money home every month, for rent, school fees and family businesses. Much of that money still moves through cash counters, in a language that is not the sender’s own. OSON X, the UAE app from OSON, is built to close that gap.

Remittances to Uzbekistan reached $18.9 billion in 2025, up 27% from $14.8 billion in 2024 and more than three times the 2020 level of $6 billion, according to the Central Bank of Uzbekistan. About 78% still comes from Russia; at the same time, a growing share now arrives from Kazakhstan, Turkey, South Korea, the United Kingdom and the European Union, as the map of where people from Central Asia work widens.

The UAE sits inside that shift. Dubai alone is home to more than 4.8 million residents (Dubai Data and Statistics Establishment, September 2026), the large majority of them expatriates, and the Central Asian community is part of that mix.

OSON X helps people from Central Asia send money, pay and use a card in one app, in Uzbek, Russian and English. It runs on one corridor: transfers between the UAE and Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, in both directions. Transfers usually arrive within minutes when sent by card or IBAN within a country, and take one to two days for international account-to-account transfers.

“The demand on this corridor is real and growing, and the people sending money deserve tools that are built for them. We built OSON X for that community, and we are at the Dubai FinTech Summit to find the partners who want to build this corridor with us,” said Makhmudov Farkhod, Founder & CEO, OSON.

OSON X is in a pilot with a limited group of users, so partners who join now can help shape the product. OSON X is looking for banking and infrastructure partners to build the UAE–Central Asia corridor together.

Meet the OSON X team at Dubai FinTech Summit, 2–3 November, stand 12.

About OSON X

OSON X is the UAE app from OSON that helps people from Central Asia send money, pay and use a card in one app, in Uzbek, Russian and English. Made for digital Nomads. It is in a pilot with a limited group of users. OSON X is operated by Oson DIFC Limited, regulated by the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA), reference F006764.

Soika Labs Launches Mockingjay Network, an Agentic AI Operating System That Lets Businesses Command Their Own AI Workforce

📅 Oct 31, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Unveiled at the Dubai AI Festival, the desktop-first platform lets businesses build, deploy and connect AI agents across a global network with early-access UAE users receiving 5,000 free credits.

Dubai, United Arab Emirates, 31st October 2026, ZEX PR WIRE — Soika Labs has opened early access to Mockingjay Network, an agentic AI operating system that lets any business build, run and command its own workforce of AI agents. Co-founder and CEO Enzo Amur unveiled the platform’s move into production at the Dubai AI Festival on 27 October, launching with a UAE-first soft rollout that gives early-access users 5,000 free credits to start building.

One platform where AI agents work as a team

An AI agent is a digital worker software that carries out real business tasks such as answering customers, qualifying and sorting leads, or standing up an entire CRM system. Most AI tools, however, operate in isolation, leaving teams to pay for several products and stitch the results together by hand. Mockingjay Network brings all of that into a single environment. Inside a company, agents work together as a coordinated team; beyond it, they connect with agents from other organisations worldwide through the Global Agentic Neural Network (GANN) to get work done faster. Each company’s private agents stay sovereign, plugging into the wider network without exposing internal data.

No code, your models, your machines

Mockingjay is built to be used without writing a line of code or hiring engineers, and it can run on a company’s own computers so sensitive data stays under its control. The platform is also one of the largest LLM aggregators available, giving users access to Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude, Kimi and more from a single place. An intelligent auto-routing system directs each task to the best-suited model saving up to 70% of credits while agents work across text, images and data. Mockingjay is delivered as a desktop application that businesses install and run locally.

Built for small and medium businesses first

Mockingjay is designed for small and medium-sized businesses before anyone else, and the opportunity is vast: an estimated 1.3 million SMEs in the UAE, around 2 million across the wider GCC, and some 36.2 million small businesses in the United States. Many want to adopt AI but find it too expensive or too complicated. Mockingjay is built to close that gap, bringing agentic AI within practical reach of leaner teams.

People stay in command

For all its automation, Mockingjay is designed around human oversight. Soika Labs sets a baseline of at least one person per division and expects “human in the loop” to become a profession of its own as businesses scale. “The rules of communication, cooperation and equality between AI agents are what make a shared network work,” said Enzo Amur, Co-founder and CEO of Soika Labs. “We want businesses to let AI do more so people can be more without letting AI take over.” The launch aligns with the UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031, as businesses across the region move from adopting AI tools to applying them for measurable operational value.

Availability and early access

Mockingjay Network is available now as a desktop application. Businesses can download it and start building their AI agents and fleets at https://www.mockingjaynetwork.com/download. As part of the UAE-first soft launch, early-access users receive 5,000 free credits. “This is the beginning of a network where businesses of every size build their own AI workforce and connect it to the world,” added Amur.

About Soika Labs

Soika Labs is a Dubai-based AI company and the team behind Mockingjay Network. Built on the principle that in the era of AI being human matters more, it develops agentic AI infrastructure that keeps businesses and people in control.

Dataline Raises $10.6M to Give AI Agents Data They Can Trust

📅 Oct 31, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →
  • Dataline announced a $10.6 million funding round alongside the initial cohort of AI Data Launch partners, marking a major step toward becoming the data lifeline in the era of AI.

Road Town, BVI, October 31, 2026, ZEX PR WIRE — The round was co-led by Lattice and Samsung-backed Dispersion Capital, with participation from AI fund Symbolic Capital. Dataline also drew a deep bench of strategic backers spanning web2 and web3, including Coinbase Ventures, Anagram, a former Head of the CFTC, and founders and partners from Robinhood, Venmo, Anchorage, NEA, General Catalyst, Jump Capital, and FalconX.

The Data Launch cohort brings together a roster of leading AI and web3 projects to establish the best data for AI, including Kite, Aerodrome, B3OS, Sentient, Sahara, Hyperliquid, Polymarket, Kalshi, Primus, Cluster, Apro, Base, Robinhood Chain, BNB, Sui, TON, and others. As part of the launch, Dataline co-announced with Base and Robinhood Chain that builders on both chains will get free Dataline access.

The raise builds on early traction that has already validated demand for the network. To date, Dataline has powered 19.4 million onchain transactions with a 96.4% agent task success rate and grown a community of more than 300,000 people worldwide. The protocol was also named a winner of the 2025 BNB Chain AI Hackathon.

Community participation is growing alongside network usage. Dataline’s first quest with Legion drew over 1,000 unique participants, who completed over 750 quests and over 1,000 raids. Quest 2 begins October 15, providing the community with another chance of earning rewards. In November, Dataline plans to hold a Uniswap Continuous Clearing Auction (CCA) on Base and on Robinhood Chain.

OpenRouter for data

Autonomous AI agents are only as good as the strength of the data behind them. Dataline is the decentralized network for agent-payable data, providing a two-sided marketplace where anyone can publish a feed and any agent can pay per call with x402. Just as OpenRouter is the routing layer for AI tokens, Dataline is the routing layer for AI data. Via a single integration, every API response carries an AI confidence score weighing source reliability, freshness, and consistency, so agents can flag or refuse bad data before acting on it.

Bringing more data online

In addition to Dataline’s curated and verified feeds, the protocol also lets anyone publish data and price it per call, like a job board for data where AI agents and humans alike can post and pick up work. A requester posts a bounty for the data they need, and any fulfiller in the network claims it, supplies the data, and gets paid. Payments settle instantly through x402, sellers’ credentials never leave the gateway, and an optional zero-knowledge attestation tier lets providers attach a verifiable proof bundle to every response.

Quality is enforced economically rather than by any central authority. Fulfillers stake tokens to submit their responses: good data earns the bounty, while bad data gets the stake slashed. The result is a constantly expanding marketplace of cross-verified, custom-fetched data on demand.

Data is the lifeblood of AI

“After building AI agents ourselves, we realized that clean and reliable data is the lifeblood of AI,” said Nuo Shi, cofounder of Dataline. “Today’s AI is capable enough to know what data it needs, sometimes better than we do. So we built an open network that not only delivers the most reliable data streams, but also lets AI request help to gather the data it can’t reach on its own.”

About Dataline

Dataline is the decentralized data network for AI agents, providing one integration for all markets. The protocol delivers cross-verified data sources with AI-generated confidence scores, along with a network of custom-fetched data requests to power a smarter AI workforce.

A Better Life Through Ai Wheel Mobility Scooter 20 inch Boarding Luggage: Airwheel Smart Carry on hand Luxury Cabin Suitcase Shine at the 140th Canton Fair

GUANGZHOU, China, October 31, 2026 — The third phase of the 140th China Import and Export Fair (Canton Fair) officially opened on October 31, bringing together global buyers seeking innovative products for modern lifestyles and travel. Airwheel, a smart mobility brand, is showcasing its range of rideable electric luxury suitcase, attracting attention from international buyers with products that combine electric mobility, intelligent features, and practical luggage storage.

By integrating electric riding capabilities into the familiar cabin suitcase format, Airwheel is exploring new ways to make everyday travel more convenient, flexible, and enjoyable.

Strong Interest from International Buyers on Opening Day

From the opening hours of the exhibition, Airwheel’s booth welcomed a steady stream of international buyers. Drawn by the distinctive concept of a suitcase that can also be ridden, visitors stopped to explore the products, ask questions, and experience the riding functions firsthand. Some buyers also expressed purchasing interest during on-site discussions.

Throughout the exhibition area, visitors could be seen trying Airwheel’s electric suitcases, experiencing a different approach to moving through large exhibition halls. The combination of riding and conventional luggage functions offers an alternative to traditional suitcases that rely entirely on pulling or pushing, making Airwheel a notable attraction in the luggage and travel products section.

Beyond its distinctive appearance, Airwheel’s smart electric cabin suitcase is designed around practical travel needs. It retains the essential storage function of conventional luggage while incorporating an electric riding system. In suitable environments, users can ride the suitcase to reduce the effort associated with long walks through airport terminals, large exhibition centers, and other spacious venues. When riding is unnecessary or unsuitable, the suitcase can be used in conventional push-and-pull mode, allowing users to adapt to changing surroundings.

Selected models also feature app-based controls, location-related functions, and ambient lighting, bringing connected technology into the travel experience. The 20inch cabin-size design enables convenient carry-on travel. Its 73.26Wh removable lithium battery has passed multiple international certifications and meets aviation boarding standards.

One Smart Suitcase, Multiple Everyday Applications

Airwheel’s rideable suitcase concept extends beyond the airport. By combining luggage storage with electric mobility, the products are designed to support different travel scenarios, from business trips and shopping excursions to everyday journeys.

Airport Mobility, Reinvented

Long airport corridors, transfers between terminals, and walks to distant boarding gates can make air travel physically demanding. Airwheel’s riding and conventional rolling modes give users greater flexibility when moving through appropriate areas.The 20-inch cabin-size format creates a practical airport boarding suitcase for air travellers.

 

Business Travel Without Limits

For professionals attending international exhibitions, conferences, and business meetings, moving efficiently between destinations is an important part of the travel experience. From airports and hotels to convention centers and exhibition halls, Airwheel’s electric suitcase provides an alternative way to move while carrying clothing, business documents, laptops, and other travel essentials.

At the Canton Fair, visitors can experience the products directly in a large exhibition environment, gaining a clearer understanding of how rideable luggage may fit into business travel routines.

Smarter Shopping and Leisure Mobility

Large shopping malls, commercial complexes, and suitable open spaces offer other potential applications for rideable luggage. Users can carry personal belongings and shopping items in the suitcase while choosing between riding and conventional rolling according to the distance, surroundings, and their own preferences.

When entering crowded areas or spaces where riding is not permitted, users can switch to conventional luggage handling. This flexibility extends the potential use of smart rideable suitcases beyond airports and railway stations to shopping, leisure, and urban exploration. 

Effortless Everyday Travel

Innovation does not have to mean abandoning familiar habits. Airwheel’s smart suitcases retain the basic storage functionality of conventional luggage, with a telescopic handle and rolling wheels for everyday handling when electric riding is not needed.

Depending on the model, users can also access features such as app-based controls, location-related functions, and lighting options. By combining familiar luggage operation with additional mobility capabilities, Airwheel aims to make intelligent technology a practical part of everyday travel.

Technology Designed Around Better Travel Experiences

Interest at the Airwheel booth reflects growing curiosity about products that combine conventional travel essentials with new mobility capabilities. For travelers who regularly navigate large airports, exhibition venues, and other expansive environments, the value of a smart suitcase lies not only in its appearance but also in how it can address everyday travel challenges.

Airwheel’s approach focuses on making luggage more adaptable to different journeys: reducing the physical effort associated with long-distance movement, maintaining practical storage capacity, and offering users greater flexibility in how they move.

This philosophy aligns naturally with the third phase of the Canton Fair and its emphasis on products that contribute to a better quality of life. A more enjoyable journey is not simply about reaching a destination; it is also about making the experience along the way more comfortable and convenient.

By bringing electric drive systems and intelligent features into a familiar travel product, Airwheel continues to explore how smart mobility technology can improve the way people travel.

A Broader Smart Rideable Suitcase Portfolio for Global Markets

At the third phase of the 140th Canton Fair, Airwheel is presenting a broad portfolio of smart rideable suitcases designed for different users and travel scenarios.

The lineup includes the SE3S series of 20-inch smart rideable cabin suitcase, the 24-inch SE3T electric rideable checked Ai wheel suitcase, and the SQ3/SQ3S children’s rideable Kids suitcase. Together, these products address a range of needs, from everyday mobility and airport travel to longer trips and family outings.

Supported by a portfolio of more than 600 global patents, Airwheel continues to develop technologies in electric drive systems, motion control, and intelligent sensing. Its products have also received recognition from international design and innovation programs, including the MUSE Design Awards, French design awards, Asian Design Awards, and iLuxury Awards.

The strong interest at the exhibition provides opportunities for Airwheel to engage with international buyers, exchange market insights, and explore potential business partnerships.

Meet Airwheel at the 140th Canton Fair

As Airwheel continues to develop products for different users and travel scenarios, its focus remains on combining practical design with intelligent mobility technology. From airport terminals and business exhibitions to shopping trips and leisure travel, the brand aims to make luggage a more versatile companion for exploring the world.

Airwheel invites international buyers, distributors, and business partners to visit its booths during the third phase of the 140th Canton Fair to experience its smart rideable suitcase portfolio firsthand and discuss potential cooperation opportunities.

A five-star hotel that never opened is sending its bespoke interiors to auction. In November, Pro Auction will sell unused furnishings commissioned for The Other House’s planned Covent Garden Residents’ Club, including pieces for 149 guestrooms and its public spaces. Some items remain in their original packaging, from fluted-oak cabinetry and sculptural lounge chairs to marble dining tables and statement lighting. The three-day sale offers buyers a rare chance to acquire a coordinated hotel collection before it ever welcomed guests. Pro Auction will sell bespoke contents commissioned for The Other House’s Wellington Block scheme, a planned five-star Residents’ Club that never opened to the public.

London, United Kingdom, 31st Oct 2026 – Pro Auction will auction the unused furnishings and decorative contents commissioned for The Other House’s planned Covent Garden Residents’ Club. The property, at 25–31 Wellington Street, was in the final stages of completion and scheduled to open in July 2026 as the flagship sister property to The Other House South Kensington. It did not open to the public.

The sale follows Aendre Group’s acquisition of The Other House group and the incoming owners’ decision to pursue a different design vision. Contents from 149 guestrooms and the property’s public spaces will be offered for sale. Some lots remain in their original factory crating, transit wraps and protective covers.

The collection was curated by The Other House’s in-house interior design department, TOHID, in collaboration with Bergman Design House, led by Marie Soliman and Albin Berglund. Items include bespoke upholstered and fluted timber headboards, curved two-seater sofas, fluted club chairs, fluted-oak storage cabinets and hallway consoles with brass inlays and soft-close hardware.

Public-area lots include sculptural lounge chairs and bespoke bistro and large-format dining tables with polished marble, terrazzo or dark-stained timber surfaces on cast-brass and cast-iron bases. The collection also includes restaurant furnishings, sculptures, fine art, decorative objects and architectural lighting. The hotel specification includes Crib 5 fire-rated items and BREEAM Excellent environmental compliance.

The sale offers hotel operators, developers, interior designers, restaurateurs, build-to-rent operators and private buyers the opportunity to acquire coordinated furnishings. The Other House South Kensington opened in 2022 as a Residents’ Club for members and overnight guests. Aendre Group, founded by Eric Jafari and Chris Strong, acquired The Other House group in July 2026.

Simon Rose of Pro Auction said: “Usually, an auction of this scale follows the conclusion of an established operational lifecycle. To step into an iconic Covent Garden island site that was on the threshold of its July 2026 debut and find thousands of pieces from Europe’s top-tier luxury manufacturers—spanning both private guestrooms and magnificent public lounges—that have never been used, never been scratched, and remain in immaculate condition is unheard of. It is an extraordinary opportunity for developers, operators, and design professionals alike.”

The auction will be held as a live and online webcast, with global bidding through major auction platforms. Viewing and digital walkthroughs will be available by appointment.
